standing: DRAFT - PROPOSED, TEST-ONLY: our proposal of a revised configuration for High Press Escape (A02-HPE2), for Christian's ecological review beside the baseline A02-HPE1; not knowledge, not approved, never served. Read only by the TEST-ONLY PROPOSED loader (back/src/system/derivation/draft-store.ts loadProposedRealization), in unit tests; no route reads it, and nothing here is in contracts.json, corpus-restatements.json, provisional-realizations.json or learning-goal-authorizations.json.
about: Package 5, the A02 ecological revision (13 November 2026), on Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 11. HPE-2 is the structural repair of HPE-1 with no added reward (candidate S of the package's comparison, refined), built at review level beside HPE-1, which stays intact as the baseline. What changes against HPE-1: the pressing team's target is an end zone at the escaping team's end, 6 m deep (ILLUSTRATIVE), entered under control (its own event target_zone_entered; Q2); the ball over an end line goes to the team that did not touch it last (the possession game's own award, GF2-16.a), restarted from the feet, the escaping team as at the start and the pressing team on the marked line (Q6); the start and the restart after each point are taken near the escaping team's own end, outside the end zone, and no longer say 'set to press together'; the coach may restart as at the start (A01's coach-judged restart reused, said by the engine in its own broader words; Q6); the teams change ends with the roles, so the markings stay (B10 EXCHANGED; Q5); the escaping team's point is read as the crossing that escapes the press (the origin and progression values of the draft store a02-hpe2-composition; Q4). Kept from HPE-1: the roles held for a block, the coach calling the next block (no block length can be stated: Q5), the one full-width line placed by a rule (12 m ILLUSTRATIVE), the escaping team's zone beyond it, no offside as the isolated review assumption (the laws block; Q3). Not built: any regain reward (A, B, C), an also-counts element for a ball won inside the end zone (E9), the block clock, the opponents' distance at a restart (no register row), normal Law 11. Every item is AUTHORED so it establishes what it proposes, and its category, stamped by the loader, says what it is: PROPOSED, or ILLUSTRATIVE for the schematic distances. No library constraint, no environmental manipulation (K2's empty set stands), no participant placement, no departure from the Laws on any item.

questions.asks: The roles and the line (missing relationship M2, what the marked line stands for; Decision 3): one team escapes and one presses for a block, with one full-width line near the escaping team's end placed by a rule, not a distance (where the pressing team, working together near that end, can just cover the width, with room beyond it to receive and keep the ball); the escaping team's target is everything beyond the line, and its point is read as the crossing that escapes the press the attempt began under (the ball dribbled over the line, or received and controlled beyond it, and kept through the team's next action). Christian kept the roles and their exchange as a review-level candidate and did not approve the line's placement or the expansive zone as canonical knowledge (received 13 November 2026); built here only as that candidate. The other answer to M2, a target limited in depth beyond the line, gates or a target player (a GF2 knowledge decision, NEW), is the next lever only if long-ball bypass dominates in review.
questions.askedFor: "I am comfortable retaining asymmetric escaping and pressing roles as a review-level candidate, including exchanging roles between blocks." (received 13 November 2026)

questions.asks: The pressing team's event (missing relationship M1, with E9; Decision 3): an end zone at the escaping team's end, across the full width, 6 m deep (ILLUSTRATIVE), entered under control (target_zone_entered: a player dribbles in, or receives and controls the ball inside it), live whenever the pressing team has the ball. No RPC-002 row authorizes an event for the opposing role, so it is carried at review level as one pending entry. Whether a ball won and controlled inside the end zone counts by itself (E9) is open and not built: needed before the coach text is used with players.
questions.askedFor: "I'd like the next package to examine whether a more coherent relationship between defensive rewards, attacking targets and possession consequences would better support the learning intention." (received 13 November 2026)

questions.asks: LAW-11 in this activity (Decision 5, after ecological review): no offside, said once to the coach, kept only as the isolated review assumption Christian permits (built as PROPOSED, the laws block). The other answers, described and not built: the default Law 11 with a marked halfway line (NEW in the engine), or a target-form change beyond the line (a GF2 knowledge decision, NEW); whether the default Law 11 is the kind of positional rule Christian declined (a rule dictating where attacking players must stand) is Christian's call. Ecological review counts long-ball points by kind (a receiver parked beyond the line; a pressing player parked in the end zone).
questions.askedFor: "For now, no offside may remain an isolated review assumption, but I am not approving it as a general A02 rule." (received 13 November 2026)

questions.asks: A crossing after the press has dropped off (Decision 4, needed before the coach text is used with players): (a) a crossing in an attempt that began under the press counts unless the escaping team lost the ball or play stopped in between, the coach judging a later score unrelated only after a long hold behind the line; or (b) the coach judges, on each attempt, whether the press was broken or withdrew unbeaten. No item waits on it: the origin value (a02-hpe2-composition) stays neutral, our CANDIDATE restatement of Christian's refinement with its closing words ('by this crossing') PROPOSED, and the coach's judgment carries the case until Christian decides.
questions.askedFor: "Facing coordinated pressure earlier in possession should not automatically qualify an unrelated later scoring event." (received 13 November 2026)

questions.asks: The lead state, in both roles (Decision 1): a team that leads can keep the problem from emerging (as the pressing team by sitting off, or pressing with one or two players; as the escaping team by long relief balls). HPE-2 changes ends with the roles (B10 EXCHANGED) and the coach calls the next block; the clock proposed for it (every 3 minutes, ILLUSTRATIVE, Decision 1 (d)) cannot be represented, because the exchange row holds only COACH_CALLS and the register grounds that closed list in Christian's A01 ruling that no new block-duration system is needed (A01 scope), so it is not built: whether a coach's regular call may stand in for it, and whether that A01 ruling reaches A02, is Christian's. Only a knowledge change reaches the state itself (Decision 1 (c)).
questions.askedFor: "If both teams understand the rules and genuinely attempt to win, do their available opportunities and incentives make the intended learning problem likely to emerge?" (received 13 November 2026)

questions.asks: The restart arrangement (PROPOSED; a proposal Christian invited, coach-adjustable, not a decision needed before review): the start, the restart after each point and the coach's restart are the escaping team's, from the feet, near its own end, outside the end zone, where the coach chooses; the ball over an end line goes to the team that did not touch it last (the possession game's own award, GF2-16.a; no item writes it), restarted from the feet, the escaping team as at the start and the pressing team on the marked line, where the coach chooses. The engine says the coach's restart broadly (whenever the coach decides an attack has run its course, at a stoppage or while play is on): the narrower trigger proposed (the escaping team with the ball beyond the line and not pressed; never while the pressing team has the ball) cannot be said and is not a rule here. The ball over a side line and fouls keep the Laws; no item writes the restart policy row, so the kick-off (LAW-8) stays owed (PROCEDURAL under our DRAFT reading, reported). The opponents' distance at a restart from the feet (as at a free kick) has no register row and is not represented. A qualifying sequence also begins in live play, after turnovers; a restart never stands in for the pressure condition, which the coach still judges in play.
questions.askedFor: "Please propose a simple, practical restart arrangement compatible with the selected scoring structure and intended game problem." (received 13 November 2026)
